content:
anya: Heads-up — Spruce is seeing intermittent 429s + a handful of 401 auth errors on their dedicated pool starting ~03:00 UTC. Customer says spikes correlate with marketing traffic. Logs attached in support ticket.
samir: Can you paste their baseline/peak QPS and current pool sizing? Need rough numbers to triage.
anya: Baseline ~120 qps steady. Yesterday peak burst reached ~720 qps for ~6 minutes. Dedicated pool = 4 GPUs (g5x2-style virtual), target_utilization configured to 75%.
olivia: Auto-scale policy looks like max_replicas=6, scale_out_cooldown=300s, target_utilization=75%. If they hit 720 qps that's ~180 qps/GPU => seems above our perf target at that seq len.
julian: Infra alert showed CPU/GPU memory okay but request queueing spiked. infra-bot: "[alert] spruce-dedicated: queue_latency_p50=320ms, 429_rate=9% over 10m"
matt: 401s are suspicious — likely token verification upstream timing out when queueing increases. Could be auth proxy timeouts (default 3s) tripping under backpressure.
anya: Repro steps customer sent:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
```
they see ~9% 429s during burst.
samir: Immediate mitigation options: 1) bump pool to 6 GPUs (add 2) 2) increase max_replicas to 8 and lower target_utilization to 65% 3) enable short-term burst_headroom (+20% traffic padding) and increase auth proxy timeout to 8s.
julian: Agree. Also validate noisy neighbor: check per-tenant GPU utilization and per-worker QPS. Run:
```
redwood infra metrics query --pool spruce-dedicated --group-by tenant
```
if one tenant dominates, consider tenant throttling/backpressure.
olivia: Quick check: tenant 'spruce-batch' had a 5m window at 62% of pool QPS, rest were 38% — not a classic noisy neighbor but heavy concurrent small requests.
matt: If requests are small, batching might help. Recommend enabling aggressive batching for that model and raising max_batch_tokens.
ops: Opening escalation ticket with priority P1 and assigning to eng-runtime and infra. ops:request_id 98342.
anya: Customer asked for ETA on pool resize. ops, can we spin 2 GPUs as emergency scale? We have capacity in us-west-2.
ops: Kicking off resize now, estimated 12 min. Also applying temporary auth proxy timeout bump to 8s and enabling burst_headroom=20%.
infra-bot: "[action] resize_started: spruce-dedicated -> 6 GPUs (req 98342)"
anya: Will monitor. I'll paste post-resize metrics in this thread.
samir: Post-mitigation follow-up: we should recommend long-term changes: set target_util=65%, max_replicas=8, add warmup traffic for predictable campaigns, and create an evergreen batching profile for their workload.
anya: Noted. Will include config diff and runbook for Spruce in the ticket. :thumbsup:
julian: Also suggest adding an SLA-safe fallback model (smaller quantized variant) to route during saturation.
matt: I'll own the fallback rollout. Will coordinate canary once ops confirms capacity stable.
anya: Closing loop for now — ops please post last metrics here when done.
ops: Done — resize finished, queue_latency_p50 down to 48ms, 429_rate <0.5% after 15m. Leaving this thread open for verification.
